subject: mathematics
question_text: If A + B + C = 0, then prove that sin 2A + sin 2B + sin 2C = −4 sin A sin B sin C.

mark_split.label: Replace cos C inside the bracket

verification.note: Source: Baby Bullet-Q, Junior Inter Maths-1A (Sri Publishers, Machilipatnam), book p.108 — from the book's separate "STAR QUESTIONS PLUS" bank, answer 169. That bank (book pp.98-111, answers 142-180) sits AFTER all the numbered chapters and is organised by chapter rather than forming part of any chapter's own inventory; it is authored into this unit because that is where the question belongs on the paper (founder decision 2026-08-22). SECTION: classed LAQ on its length and shape — a transformation identity on a triangle, the exact shape of Unit 6's own LAQ chapter. The bank prints no mark cut, so this classification is OURS. Printed appearances: AP 19. The condition is ZERO, not π. That is what puts the minus sign on the right-hand side, and it appears at a single identifiable step. ⚠ THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S — the bank prints no [N Marks] tags anywhere. The shapes used follow the splits the book DOES print elsewhere: 1+1 for a 2-mark VSAQ (answers 100, 101 on book p.82), 1+1+1+1 or 1+2+1 for a 4-mark SAQ (answers 58, 59 on p.63 and 61 on p.64), and the granular split for a 7-mark LAQ (answer 32 on p.44). This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would do this one — name each move in order.

steps.label: Group the first two terms
steps.margin_note: Two of the seven marks. sin C + sin D = 2 sin((C+D)/2) cos((C−D)/2), applied to sin 2A + sin 2B.

recall.must_convey: That sin 2A + sin 2B becomes 2 sin(A+B) cos(A−B).
accept: group the first two and apply sin C plus sin D to get two sin of A plus B into cos of A minus B
apply the sum to product formula to the first pair
the halves cancel the twos
modati rendu group chesi sum to product
convert the first pair to a product

steps.why: Note the shape: for a sum of SINES the sine takes the sum and the cosine takes the difference. For cosines it is the other way round.
common_mistakes: Using the cos C + cos D formula.
Putting the cosine on the sum.

steps.label: Replace A + B by −C
steps.margin_note: Third mark, and where the minus sign first appears. A + B = −C, and sin(−C) = −sin C.
lines: L.H.S = −2 sin C cos(A − B) + sin 2C

recall.must_convey: That A + B = −C gives sin(A+B) = −sin C, introducing the minus sign.
accept: A plus B is minus C and sine of minus C is minus sin C
the sine is an odd function so the minus comes out
this is where the minus sign on the answer comes from
A plus B ante minus C, sin minus C ante minus sin C
apply the zero sum condition

steps.why: sin(−θ) = −sin θ, so the minus comes straight out. That single sign is the minus in the final answer.
common_mistakes: Using A + B = π − C out of habit.

steps.label: Expand sin 2C and factor
steps.margin_note: Two marks. sin 2C = 2 sin C cos C, so both terms now carry 2 sin C — take it out, keeping the minus outside.
lines: L.H.S = −2 sin C cos(A − B) + 2 sin C cos C

recall.must_convey: That sin 2C = 2 sin C cos C, and −2 sin C is factored out leaving cos(A−B) − cos C.
accept: sin two C is two sin C cos C and taking minus two sin C out leaves cos A minus B minus cos C
both terms have two sin C so factor it out
keep the minus sign outside the bracket
sin two C ante two sin C cos C, minus two sin C common teeyali
expand the double angle and factor

steps.why: Taking out −2 sin C rather than +2 sin C flips the sign of the second term inside — which is what sets up the difference formula next.
common_mistakes: Factoring +2 sin C and getting the bracket signs the wrong way round.
Writing sin 2C = sin C cos C.

steps.label: Replace cos C inside the bracket
steps.margin_note: Sixth mark. Inside the bracket, cos C = cos(−(A+B)) = cos(A+B), because cosine ignores the sign.
lines: Inside the bracket, C = −(A + B), so
cos C = cos(−(A + B)) = cos(A + B)

recall.must_convey: That cos C = cos(A + B) inside the bracket, since cos(−θ) = cos θ.
accept: cos C equals cos of A plus B because cosine ignores the sign
cos of minus theta is cos theta so the minus disappears here
the bracket becomes cos A minus B minus cos A plus B
cos minus theta ante cos theta, so cos C ante cos A plus B
substitute inside the bracket

steps.why: The cosine is even, so no minus appears here — unlike the sine in step 2. Knowing which function keeps the sign is the whole difference.
common_mistakes: Converting the sin C outside as well.

steps.label: Apply the difference formula
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos(X−Y) − cos(X+Y) = 2 sin X sin Y with X = A, Y = B gives 2 sin A sin B.
lines: cos(A − B) − cos(A + B) = 2 sin A sin B
L.H.S = −2 sin C · 2 sin A sin B

lines.text: ∴ sin 2A + sin 2B + sin 2C = −4 sin A sin B sin C

recall.must_convey: That the bracket is 2 sin A sin B, giving −4 sin A sin B sin C.
accept: the bracket is two sin A sin B so the answer is minus four sin A sin B sin C
multiply by minus two sin C to get minus four
the two twos give four and the minus is carried through
bracket two sin A sin B, minus two sin C tho multiply cheste minus four
apply the difference formula and close

steps.why: The minus has been carried from step 2 to here without changing. Tracking one sign through five steps is what this proof is really testing.
common_mistakes: Dropping the minus at the last line.
Writing the bracket as 2 cos A cos B.
